tells: 1. Laugh onset barely reads: across 1.0 s only the white-cardigan woman lifts a hand to her chest and a couple of heads turn; no shoulder heave, no torso pitch-back, no shared contagion, the other five front-row bodies hold the same listening pose frame to frame (club-5-strip.png, whole front row, frames t=12.0-13.0)

2. Face close is a game-engine head: waxy uniform orange skin with no pores or specular breakup, glassy dead eyes with no wet line or eyelid occlusion, mouth shape is a blendshape not a laugh, and a dark cutout halo around the shoulder/hair against the blurred bokeh (club-4-face.png, face center and silhouette edge)

3. Same Rocketbox cast cloned through the room: magenta tracksuit guy, teal hoodie guy, purple-top woman and blonde-crop woman appear in every shot with identical posture families; seated people all square to the stage with hands parked on tables in mirrored pairs (club-1-wide.png front row; club-3-mid.png center)

4. Back of house is flat black cardboard silhouettes standing in haze with no internal shading, no seats, no motion and identical heights; reads as a matte painting (club-1-wide.png, mid band behind front tables; club-2-mid.png upper left)

5. Contact: hands hover on table tops without weight or deformation, forearms intersect table edge, glasses unheld, legs under tables vanish into black, and hair is solid helmet geometry with no strand breakup or rim fringe (club-6-held.png, teal hoodie hands and purple-top woman hair; club-2-mid.png, table center)

1. Seated bodies float: the front row sit upright with straight spines, thighs level above the seat cushions, hands clamped on knees in near-identical poses, and seat backs show through/behind them with no compression; rows 2-3 look like standing mannequins poking up between seat backs (theatre-1-wide.png, front two rows; theatre-3-mid.png, center row)

2. Laugh is a mouth-open switch, not a build: in the strip mouths snap open on a few people between t=12.6 and t=12.8 while torsos, shoulders and heads stay rigid; the only big move is the teal-hoodie guy bringing hands together at t=13.0 and the far-right guy pitching his head down in one frame, with no breath-driven heave or rocking (theatre-5-strip.png, front row, frames 4-6)

3. Face close: shaved-blonde woman with flat dark mouth interior (no teeth or tongue visible), plastic beige skin, rubbery cheek shape, eyes not converged on anything, earrings clipping the jaw line; laugh reads as a gasp (theatre-4-face.png, face and mouth)

4. Hair is the biggest giveaway in the held frame: blonde bun is a hard card silhouette with jagged alpha fringe, the man's cap merges into his skull, the back rows have identical helmet hair; no flyaways or light transmission (theatre-6-held.png, blonde bun center-right and cap left)

5. Back stands are a grid of duplicated low-LOD figures at identical poses and spacing, half-lit silhouettes in blue haze, nobody slumped, leaning, whispering or on a phone; the tiering repeats like a texture (theatre-1-wide.png, upper two-thirds; theatre-2-mid.png, upper band)

1. Bodies hover and pinch: people sit with no visible chair under them, knees and thighs at the same height for the whole row, hands resting palm-down on thighs in mirrored copies, and the front woman's legs read as bare pink cylinders; nobody is slouched, cross-legged or turned (openmic-1-wide.png, front row lower half; openmic-3-mid.png, lower third)

2. Strip shows the best life of the three (green-tee woman turns to her neighbour, brown-haired woman leans in, the afro guy opens his mouth) but it is still head-and-jaw only: shoulders don't rise, chests don't pump, nobody claps, slaps a knee or covers their mouth, and the men on the left are stone still for all six frames (openmic-5-strip.png, left half and center, t=12.0-13.0)

3. Face close: plastic sheen skin, eyes painted flat with no moisture or lid shadow, mouth a straight closed line on a man supposedly in a laughing room, and the hairline dissolves into a pixel-dithered fringe at the back of the head (openmic-4-face.png, hair at upper right and eyes)

4. Lighting: the row of identical ceiling discs with perfect bokeh halos, a flat brown wall and a single green exit dot read as a game level; faces in the front are lit evenly with no falloff from a stage key, and no one casts a shadow on a neighbour (openmic-1-wide.png, upper band; openmic-6-held.png, faces)

5. Cast repetition and costume tells: same yellow henley, green tee and burgundy tracksuit as the other venues, denim and leather with baked-in texture wrinkles that never deform as people move; the right-edge blonde woman is cropped with a hard alpha hairline (openmic-6-held.png, right edge; openmic-2-mid.png, clothes center)
